articleTitle: Wrappers and Metadata Sub Group [digital video standards]
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The EBU-SMPTE Task Force: Building an Infrastructure for Managing Compressed Video Systems (Ref. No: 1997/382)
abstract: This paper reviews the deliberations of the Task Force's Sub-Group on Wrappers and Metadata up to the present time. The initial discussions of the Sub-Group from September 1996 led to the preparation of the Wrappers and Metadata chapter of the First Report on User Requirements in April 1997. This chapter included some tutorial information defining the terminology and structure of Content within a Wrapper. It also contained a list of Requirements for Wrapper formats with explanations and descriptions, some tutorial annexes, and several specific recommendations for standardization. Ongoing work for the Wrappers Sub-Group is to prepare a final report recommending the development of standards in line with the original recommendations, based upon technologies extracted from the Request for Technology (RFT) responses, showing those areas where particular attention is required for achieving interoperation, and those areas where new specifications must be written to cover requirements not yet answered.

articleTitle: Packetised stream formats for the SDTI
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The EBU-SMPTE Task Force: Building an Infrastructure for Managing Compressed Video Systems (Ref. No: 1997/382)
abstract: With the imminent release of the serial data transport interface (SDTI) as an SMPTE standard, there is now the possibility of establishing a number of packetised formats for broadcast use. The SDTI provides only a transport layer and does not define the format of the signals carried; that is the subject of the next higher layer-SDTI formats. Some of these formats already exist in readily available equipment and some are in the process of development. The paper gives a status report of four such formats and provide details of the first.

articleTitle: The EBU-SMPTE Task Force: File Transfers Sub-group
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on The EBU-SMPTE Task Force: Building an Infrastructure for Managing Compressed Video Systems (Ref. No: 1997/382)
abstract: The File Transfer Sub-group of the Task Force was established to tackle the interoperability issues relating to asset transfers. That is, the transfer of audio, video and data between devices. This involves not only the physical connections between devices but also the protocols employed to control the flow of information. The growing use of computer-based technology in post-production has created an interest in the use of networks in programme production, initially in the area of audio editing but now also for video. Video compression techniques allowed useful amounts of material to be stored on computer disks and networking gives a number of people access to the same material. Interconnections via wide-area networks permit distributed production to take place, with specialized operations taking place where the necessary skills are located.
